Separate local learning setup from production architecture; pin reproducible installs and validate
environment.

A machine-specific install that cannot be recreated is not an operationally trustworthy setup.
C3-03-L03 — DAG authoring with TaskFlow and tasks
MENTAL MODEL
Use explicit task boundaries, dependencies and TaskFlow data passing without hiding external side
effects.
FAILURE TO CATCH
Decorators can make code concise while still creating opaque or over-coupled task boundaries.
C3-03-L04 — Schedules, logical dates and data intervals
MENTAL MODEL
Map each run to the data interval it owns; reason with logical date/data_interval rather than wall-clock
intuition.
FAILURE TO CATCH
Reading “today’s file” from current clock time causes historical reruns to process the wrong partition.
C3-03-L05 — Parameters, variables, connections and secret boundaries
MENTAL MODEL
Keep per-run parameters, deployment configuration, connection IDs and secret values in their proper
boundaries.
FAILURE TO CATCH
Hard-coded credentials or environment-specific paths leak secrets and make the DAG non-portable.
C3-03-L06 — Retries, timeouts and failure callbacks
MENTAL MODEL
Retry bounded transient failures; deterministic data/contract failures must remain failed and
diagnosable.
FAILURE TO CATCH
Retrying deterministic bad data only delays the same failure and may repeat side effects.
C3-03-L07 — Catchup, backfills and controlled reprocessing
MENTAL MODEL
Backfill historical intervals with explicit reprocessing behavior, bounded concurrency and stale-safe
target semantics.
FAILURE TO CATCH
Blind catchup can overload downstream systems or let older partitions regress newer state.
C3-03-L08 — Sensors and data-aware dependencies
MENTAL MODEL
Wait for readiness without consuming workers indefinitely; choose
poke/reschedule/deferrable/data-aware patterns deliberately.
FAILURE TO CATCH
An unbounded sensor can occupy scarce capacity while the input can never arrive.
C3-03-L09 — Idempotent task design and partial reruns
MENTAL MODEL
Every write-side effect needs a stable key/partition contract so rerunning a date/task does not duplicate
or regress state.
FAILURE TO CATCH
Append-only writes make a successful retry silently duplicate previously written records.

Page 2
Diagnostic review
INTERVAL OWNERSHIP
Each Airflow run must derive its source partition from the logical data interval. A historical run must not
read the wall-clock current file.
DAG BOUNDARIES
wait -> extract -> validate -> load/merge -> reconcile -> publish gives observable failure boundaries
and supports smallest-safe recovery.
FAILURE CLASSIFICATION
Use a bounded retry for a simulated transient failure. A deterministic validation/contract failure must
stay failed; retrying it does not fix the cause.
READINESS WAIT
Temporarily remove one packaged interval as instructed. The wait must be bounded; absence
becomes explicit evidence, not an infinite worker-consuming wait.
IDEMPOTENCE
Rerunning the same date must not duplicate the already-written event/version. Save before/after
row/key/value reconciliation.
STALE-SAFE REPROCESSING
Process 2026-11-01, then 2026-11-02, then reprocess 2026-11-01. The older partition must not
regress P8102 to its earlier version.
RESOURCE CONTROL
Use pool case_sink_small and deliberately bounded backfill concurrency; prove the sink cannot be
flooded by catchup.
TROUBLESHOOTING
Save DAG run ID, task ID, try number, logical interval and exact log evidence. Recover only the
failed/unsafe portion.
PUBLISH GATE
Publish only after partition count, unique-key/latest-state and value reconciliation all pass.
Green-but-wrong states to reject
•
All Airflow tasks are green, but the historical run read the current-date partition.
•
The sink has every raw row, but duplicate event versions make current state wrong.
•
A missing input is “handled” by returning zero rows and publishing an empty partition.
•
A whole-DAG clear repeats already-successful side effects when only one task required recovery.

historical date and show exact expected filename.
IF IDEMPOTENCE FAILED
Add stable event/key merge semantics or partition replacement contract. Changed micro-proof: rerun a
supplied date twice and prove no row/value growth.
IF STALE REPROCESS FAILED
Protect newer state using event version/update timestamp or equivalent contract. Changed
micro-proof: reprocess 2026-11-01 after 2026-11-02 and prove P8102 remains at the newer version.
IF RETRY LOGIC FAILED
Separate transient exception from deterministic data/contract error; cap retry/timeout. Changed
micro-proof: transient succeeds on bounded retry while deterministic fault remains failed.
IF WAIT/POOL FAILED
